artifacts.name: Subject features · Guided counts-independent
artifacts.describe: One saved sample per subject and selected group, joined by exact sample name to a checksum-pinned diversity result. No pooling, averaging, depth normalization, imputation or group testing. Paired rows remain linked by subject. Observed richness and diversity depend on sampling depth; Hill numbers are effective clonotype counts, Shannon entropy uses natural logarithms. Coverage estimates abundance completeness, not the fraction of all clonotypes observed. The table carries point estimates only; parent intervals describe within-sample measurement uncertainty, not between-subject uncertainty. Empty samples retain zero abundance and richness; undefined values remain missing with reasons. Design Guided counts-independent version 1 (cd-4edc30a12e0f37f1bfd6324de54fbe425e2444343cfc2bef1c5d5b7fff4e7fb0): independent groups "control" then "stimulated", 32 subjects, 32 selected observations; diversity parent div-19309e495feb626f (SHA-256 679b5b22a5999fa6d64adc6490451bd78ad3c6a0295e9a664b3177bec1025f00), definition def-fced5f1579ff (each locus separately by amino-acid junction, V gene and J gene), QC: none; abundance unit umis. All design annotations and exclusions are saved snapshots.
artifacts.citation: Jost 2006, Entropy and diversity, doi:10.1111/j.2006.0030-1299.14714.x; Chao & Jost 2012, doi:10.1890/11-1952.1; Chao et al. 2014, doi:10.1890/13-0133.1. Selection, missingness and the fixed feature catalog are ClonoLoom policies.

artifacts.name: Group comparison · Guided counts-independent
artifacts.describe: Two-group independent subject comparison: "stimulated" minus "control"; 32 subjects and 32 selected observations. Each selected feature receives a two-sided Welch t and Mann–Whitney U (comparison group). BH family: both tests for all 3 selected features (6 slots; 6 testable); untestable slots contribute p=1 but remain missing. No correction across other results, contrasts or exploratory feature selection. BH control assumes independence or suitable positive dependence; arbitrary dependence is not guaranteed. 95.0% intervals are marginal, not multiplicity-adjusted. Mean intervals use the t model; probability intervals use conservative bounded-difference bounds, not rank-test inversion or median-shift intervals. Any missing selected observation leaves that feature untested. No automatic outlier removal, transformations, pooling, covariate adjustment or depth standardization. Subjects must be independent between biological units. Welch assumes independent samples and normal means (small samples especially require plausible normality); paired t assumes normal subject differences. Mann–Whitney tests identical distributions under label exchangeability, not merely equal medians; signed-rank assumes differences symmetric about zero with exchangeable signs. Literal saved floating-point values define ties and exact zero differences. Rank tails include ties and use absolute centered rank scores, exact up to 50000 assignments, otherwise 9999 Monte Carlo draws with (tail+1)/(draws+1), seed 20261025. Plots show observed subject values, paired links and separately labeled effects; absence of significance is not equivalence or evidence of no effect. Feature parent cf-fdef7fae4323064cb38be767 (SHA-256 3e806cbeba0ee9441458efb120a779765c7d72ed93210ada5a0f3e0d1814601a); design Guided counts-independent version 1 (cd-4edc30a12e0f37f1bfd6324de54fbe425e2444343cfc2bef1c5d5b7fff4e7fb0). Dataset Simulated study (counts-independent) (d-b27666a1f9c38f39); definition def-fced5f1579ff: each locus separately by amino-acid junction, V gene and J gene; QC: none; abundance umis. Saved feature measurements remain at their observed sample depths; no diversity refitting.

artifacts.name: Replicated counts · Guided counts-independent
artifacts.describe: Replicated NB2 log-link model: variance = mean + dispersion × mean². Offset is log of all assigned clonotype counts in each selected sample, before feature filtering; effects are relative repertoire abundance, not absolute cell expansion. No composition normalization, shrinkage or Poisson fallback. Separate per-clonotype Cox–Reid dispersion estimates under the full design; nested-model likelihood-ratio p-values use an asymptotic chi-square with one degree of freedom at that fitted dispersion. Wald intervals are marginal and conditional on estimated dispersion; small-sample and dispersion-estimation uncertainty can affect calibration. Subject fixed effects block paired observations; this is not a random-effects model and assumes conditional independence after blocking. Optional batch adjustment requires a full-rank design. BH covers every count/prevalence-eligible clonotype, including failed fits as p=1 placeholders that remain displayed as unavailable. BH assumes independence or suitable positive dependence; no correction across other results or exploratory choices. Zero counts are observations, not missing data. Whole nonnegative counts and positive library totals are required. All-zero groups/subject blocks, dispersion boundaries and nonconvergence remain explicit failures. Do not infer antigen specificity or causality; independent biological units and an appropriate sampling model remain required. Design Guided counts-independent version 1 (cd-4edc30a12e0f37f1bfd6324de54fbe425e2444343cfc2bef1c5d5b7fff4e7fb0), independent: "stimulated" minus "control"; 32 subjects, 32 selected observations, 29 residual df. Feature parent cf-fdef7fae4323064cb38be767 SHA-256 3e806cbeba0ee9441458efb120a779765c7d72ed93210ada5a0f3e0d1814601a; dataset d-b27666a1f9c38f39; definition def-fced5f1579ff (each locus separately by amino-acid junction, V gene and J gene), QC none, count unit umis. Count filter >=10 in >=12 samples; BH family 48, fitted 48. 95.0% marginal Wald intervals, conditional on fitted dispersion. Batch adjustment: true.
artifacts.citation: McCarthy DJ, Chen Y, Smyth GK. Differential expression analysis of multifactor RNA-Seq experiments with respect to biological variation. Nucleic Acids Res. 2012;40:4288–4297. doi:10.1093/nar/gks042. Benjamini Y, Hochberg Y. JRSS B. 1995;57:289–300. doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x.
